question: Did it accomplish what the user asked for?

degrade.response: outcome-type requirements cannot be verified via command output → s8 marks unverifiable or degrades to artifact evidence, and flags them as uncovered in the report
degrade.timestamps: official-source Action.ts all empty → time window falls back to meta.created_at → recording file mtime (P5/P6)

controls.note: synthetic negative controls must be judged false, otherwise the whole verdict is marked INVALID

steps.purpose: delimit the search boundary + capability probe: idx_range_per_turn / written_dirs / time_window / has_response
multi-turn dialogue → list of verifiable atomic requirements (intent classification + status + strength)
validate: non-request turns must not produce requirements

steps.purpose: inject fabricated requirements that never appear in the trajectory as a built-in control group; only injected when their anchors have df=0 across the whole tree
agent replies → list of self-claims (did/produced/verified/declined), used for overclaim reconciliation
validate: quote must be a fragment from the original text

steps.purpose: requirement → hard_check (deterministic criteria) + anchors (retrieval anchors) + residual; scope filled in by code
validate: artifact_glob must not contain curly braces

steps.purpose: two tracks: hard_check exact lookup + anchors retrieve top-K. Output tri-state (hard/candidates/absent), no verdict
notes: dual query in-scope + whole-tree, out-of-scope hits marked evidence_before_request (P3)
when absent, partition anchors by df into suspect_anchors / no_scoring_action (P4)

steps.purpose: supplementary probe for absent / low-candidate requirements: same-family write actions + trajectory vocabulary samples (action distribution / command head words / files written)
notes: vocabulary samples let s8 distinguish 'wrong anchor wording' from 'really didn't do it' — both give df=0

steps.purpose: filesystem cross-check to fill trajectory blind spots (files written from inside scripts do not appear in the trajectory)
notes: file class: mtime within run time window → strong, otherwise stale
shared state (ports/processes) is always info, not evidence — cannot be attributed to this run

steps.purpose: assemble evidence bundle → per-item verdict satisfied / tier / overclaim + reason
validate: evidence_actions must be a subset of refs appearing in the evidence bundle (catch hallucinations)
each item must have a reason
notes: confidence is not given by the LLM; it is derived from the tier ceiling + presence of residual (schema.cap_confidence)

steps.purpose: only count requirements with status=active and strength=strong; if control group not caught → verdict=INVALID

verdict_rules.FAIL: there exists a strong/active requirement with satisfied=false, or an overclaim exists
verdict_rules.WEAK_PASS: no unmet requirements, but unverifiable ones exist
verdict_rules.PASS: all strong/active requirements satisfied and no overclaim
verdict_rules.INVALID: built-in control group was not judged false — verdict is too lenient, this run's result is not trustworthy
